meta.title: Nick Scali AI delivery configurator — data model

sheet.title: 2026-11-23 - Nick Scali - AI Demo
sheet.column_notes: Five columns are used (A–E) on a 28-column tab. The service-time header is spelled 'Whtite Glove Service Time' in the Sheet. Technical Specifications mostly repeats the product name (likely a hyperlink), except Tropea and Provence, where package dimensions are pasted. Rough Cubic is filled only for the Los Angeles 4-seater (value 2).
sheet.baseline_context: Service times are for white glove at a new house with no stairs and no unit or small apartment. The timer starts at a 150 m geofence.

rules_worth_using: Measure doorways (inner width, height and diagonal, doors fully open), hallways, corners, stairways (width at the narrowest point and ceiling clearance from the top and bottom steps), and lifts (door width and height, internal depth and diagonal).
Every package must pass doorways, hallways, stairwells, lifts, tight corners and turns, entry gates and pathways. Allow a few centimetres for packaging.
If a doorway is too narrow, the piece may have to go through upright, so doorway height must exceed the sofa width.

Important: some 3-seater and even 4-seater lounges are delivered in a single piece. Confirm the piece can be manoeuvred around corners and into the room, not just through the front door. This is an Access check trigger.
The customer is responsible for confirming property access and fit. If furniture will not fit in the lift or the intended room, additional fees apply.
If furniture is carried up more than two flights of stairs, a $25 fee applies for each flight after the first two.
Packaging is left with the customer. Nick Scali does not deliver on weekends. A balcony lift is the customer's responsibility.
Disassembly and reassembly, if needed for access, is a third-party service paid by the customer; not all lounges can be taken apart.

rules.geofence_note: The service timer starts when the truck comes within 150 m of the customer's residence.
rules.minimum_note: A single or swivel chair is the 15-minute minimum. By the time the driver parks, meets the customer, introduces themselves, unboxes, sets up and removes rubbish, that time is used.
rules.two_pieces_note: Dane's working rule is that two pieces, or minimal assembly, is around 30 minutes. The Sheet still times the Los Angeles 4-seater (2 pieces) and the Manchester 3-seater (2 pieces) at 15 minutes. The model uses the Sheet times as the baseline and flags this for confirmation.
rules.tables_note: Tables are fairly quick: top, legs fixed with an Allen key, then flipped. Sheet time is 30 minutes for Tropea and Provence.
rules.power_recliners_note: Power recliners take longer: power, centre consoles, and demonstrating the recliner. The Sheet times the Suffolk 3-seat dual electric at 20 minutes and the Norfolk 5-seat electric corner at 45 minutes.
rules.beds_note: Beds take longer: they usually come flat-packed, open like a butterfly, then are bolted together, with slats, bedhead and sides. Sheet time for the Ciel bed is 45 minutes.

multi_item_formula.name: Largest item in full, plus one-third of every extra item
multi_item_formula.description: Sort the line items by their white-glove base minutes. The largest item is timed in full. Each extra item adds one-third of its own base minutes. The crew is already on site, introduced, and set up, so extra pieces should not be timed as new jobs. Property modifiers are then added once per stop.

check_45_plus_45.note: A second identical 45-minute sofa takes the job to 60, not 90.

multi_item_formula.rounding: Round the item subtotal to the nearest minute, then add the property modifier.
multi_item_formula.status: Proposed formula, for Dane to confirm.

property_modifiers.status: Assumed minute values, for Dane to confirm. The Sheet baselines already assume a plain new house (0).

values.label: New house, no stairs, no unit or small apartment
Unit with stairs
values.note: Added once per floor above ground, including the first two flights. The Fit Guide's $25-per-flight fee only starts after two flights; that is a charge, not a time, and is separate.

values.label: High-rise with lift
values.note: Lift wait, booking, and long corridors. Also an Access check trigger (Fit Guide: confirm the piece fits the lift).

values.label: 3-storey house on a steep driveway
values.note: Steep carry plus internal stairs. Also an Access check trigger.

labels.defaults: The Sheet times are for White glove, so that is the default label on every configured job.
labels.white_glove_room_of_choice_assembly: White glove, room of choice and assembly can apply to any order. Room of choice does not yet have its own times, so example orders that could be room of choice still use the white-glove baseline.
labels.atl: ATL is usually for single small items, such as a swivel chair. A separate ATL time has not been given, so ATL is recorded as eligible on the Barrel armchair only, and is not used as the timed label in the example orders.
labels.assembly: Assembly is added when the work includes table legs, a flat-pack bed, or power recliner setup and demonstration.
labels.assembly_only: Assembly only is available as a label, but none of the example orders use it as the primary service.
labels.access_check: Access check is added for very large items (for example a 3 m table, an assembled length of 300 cm or more, a package of 240 cm or more, or a 10-package corner) or when the Fit Guide access path is difficult (stairs, lift, steep driveway).
labels.transfer_and_collection: Transfer (middle mile) and Collection or pickup are in the label set, but they are not used in this white-glove example batch.

truck_economics.note: These are Dane's working figures, for a typical day.

radaro_defaults.conservative_before_note: Dane's real default in smaller states, such as Adelaide.
radaro_defaults.qld_default_note: Used in QLD, where there is more geography.
radaro_defaults.sheet_example_average_check: Exact. The 10 Sheet white-glove times are 15, 45, 15, 30, 20, 20, 15, 45, 30, 30. Sum 265, average 26.5.
radaro_defaults.saving_per_driver_per_day_headline: ~100 min saved per driver, per day
radaro_defaults.saving_per_driver_per_day_note: 12 jobs × 8.5 minutes = 102 minutes, presented as about 100 minutes.

after_if_time_reinvested.note: Example only. If the recovered ~100 minutes is used for extra stops, and travel stays about 17.5 minutes a job, a 10.5-hour on-road window (07:00–17:30) could support about 14 jobs (14 × 26.5 service + 14 × 17.5 travel = 616 minutes).

batch_totals.note: The 26.5-minute average is from the 10 Sheet product baselines (new house, no modifiers), not from these 10 scenario orders. The scenario orders add property modifiers and a whole-house stop, so their average configured time is higher (397 ÷ 10 = 39.7 minutes). This example mix is 28.486 m³, just under the 30 m³ usable truck. The whole-house order alone is 8.85 m³.
